replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed items:

1. Automated abuse reachable by anyone — design has it: "The storefront uses a public GraphQL endpoint." Covered by listed threats 2 and 3 (scraping and query-cost DoS); no sign-in, email/SMS send, or sign-up exists in the design, so no brute-force/flooding variant applies.
2. Staff/admin/moderator screens showing user-supplied content — design has no such thing; it names only "nested queries of products, reviews and customer profiles" with no admin or moderation UI. Not applicable.
3. Delete/moderate/refund/role-change/money actions without a record — design describes only query capability ("Clients can request nested queries"); no mutations, no privileged actions, no audit surface stated. Not applicable.
4. Personal/financial pages cacheable by browsers, proxies or CDNs — design mentions "customer profiles" but says nothing about caching, CDN or response headers; claiming it would depend on how it is built. Not applicable.
5. Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV exports, emails or headers — design states no export, logging, email or downstream system. Not applicable.

Single-reviewer items: #1 and #5 restate listed threat 3 (scraping); #3 restates listed threat 4 (nested traversal into profiles); #2 and #4 depend on resolver implementation, batching support and the existence of a lookup token or email-existence check that the design never states. No new gap.
